Alex K: Quick sync — we need to pick a prioritization approach for billing granularity (per-token vs per-request), rate limits, and reserved-capacity SKUs. Can we do a fast RICE-style pass and call a sequencing?
Mira P: yes — quick table would help. are we optimizing for ARR or adoption velocity?
Jordan L: ARR long-term but onboarding friction kills PLG. my rough leaning: 3 tiers — dev (free/dev credits), team (PAYG w/ soft caps), reserved (commit + SLA/priority routing).
Sam: sequencing note: launch PAYG + soft caps first, then reserved contracts. infra ramp is smoother and we get product signals earlier.
Eva R: from sales calls — enterprise buyers want predictable latency + commit discounts. many will sign 6–12mo. small customers care about predictable price calc.
Alex K: propose we do a RICE-lite scoring to prioritize workstreams: billing granularity, rate-limit enforcement, reserved SKUs + contract flow. want quick estimates.
Mira P: fine. let's keep it lightweight: Impact (1–10), Effort (1–10), Confidence (1–10). I'll make a spreadsheet. note: rate limits increase infra complexity beyond just billing.
Jordan L: engineering caveat — per-token billing needs streaming aggregator + batched job for invoices; complexity jumps vs per-request. if we do per-token we should also do sampling/approximation to keep cost down.
pricing-bot: historical note: when we moved to per-second VM billing in infra, invoice processing volume spiked ~30% during rollout windows. expect similar if we change granularity.
Sam: tradeoffs: per-token = fair but expensive to implement and hard to explain. per-request = cheap but can be gamed (huge responses). hybrid option: per-request flat for outputs <256 tokens, per-token beyond that. keeps billing approachable and limits attackers.
Eva R: hybrid looks pragmatic. require a clear calculator in console + example invoices for customers. also need SLA language for reserved plans (latency percentiles, throttling guarantees).
Alex K: sketch decision path: 1) adopt hybrid PAYG billing + soft rate limits (dev-friendly, quick wins), 2) build reserved capacity SKU + contract flow, 3) later tighten into SLO-backed hard rate limits and rollout quotas. agree?
Jordan L: tentative ETA: PAYG hybrid prototyping + billing backend — ~6 sprints (inc. rollout safety). reserved API + contract flows after — +4 sprints. minimal beta for capacity routing (autopilot) is doable earlier if we scope tightly.
Mira P: I'll draft a prioritization doc and populate sample RICE scores by EOD tomorrow. will include reach assumptions and a short sequencing rationale.
Alex K: budget check — allocating 2 eng sprints for prototyping is OK with product? I'll loop finance.
Mira P: good — ping me when budget is confirmed, I can lock roadmap items. :thumbsup:
Alex K: confirmed I'll ping finance and follow up in the roadmap doc. thanks all, putting this in Q3 planning thread.
